newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan cabinet to hold post-Deng meeting on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cabinet to hold post-Deng meeting on Monday.

text.p: Taiwan's cabinet will meet on Monday to discuss the implications of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the state Central News Agency said on Saturday.
Officials from all ministries would attend the meeting, an activity the cabinet said was normal practice for "major events", the agency reported.
Talks would focus on a range of issues including China's political situation, Taiwan's national security and Taiwanese investments on the mainland in the post-Deng era, it said.
The report did not give further details.
Taiwan officials, including President Lee Teng-hui, have urged people on the island not to overreact to Deng's death.
Communist Beijing and Nationalist Taipei have been political rivals since a civil war split the two in 1949.

China threatens to attack Taiwan if the island declares independence. China's missile tests near Taiwan in early 1996, aimed at warning the island not to drop a pledge for reunification, caused widespread alarm.
